_source: Hand-verified during research: checked each state's own Secretary of State (or equivalent) site directly for a plain, static, address-free official ballot-measure document (a voter guide/pamphlet covering proposition text), not an API, not a lookup tool.
_method: Each entry here has a real, currently-or-recently-fetched document backing it and a registered parsing strategy in ballot_measures_pdf.py's STRATEGIES map. A state with no entry here still falls back to Vote Smart in election_pipeline._sync_ballot_measures — this file only ever ADDS coverage, it never removes a state's chance at data. Two ways to point at a state's PDF: 'url_pattern' (a {year}-substitutable formula, verified stable across two real elections) for states whose filename convention doesn't change; 'landing_page_url' + optional 'keyword' (discover_pdf_url in ballot_measures_pdf.py) for states that republish under a NEW filename every cycle but keep the same stable landing page and human-readable link text (e.g. 'Blue Book 2024') — this is what makes those entries evergreen without a human updating a URL each cycle.

CA.description: Official Voter Information Guide, 'Quick Reference Guide' section. Verified against the real 2024 general (144 pages, 10 real propositions) and 2026 primary (64 pages, correctly zero propositions) guides. url_pattern's {year} is substituted at fetch time; the general-election path is the only one that carries propositions.

MA.description: Official 'Information For Voters' guide. URL pattern verified stable across two real elections (2024 general, 5 real questions; 2022 general, 3 real questions) — same two-election bar CA's pattern was held to. All 8 real questions across both years parse with correct official_summary/fiscal_impact/yes_means/no_means.

CO.description: Official 'Blue Book', 'Quick Ballot Reference Guide' section. Filename changes every cycle (verified: a different one-off convention nearly every year back to 2012), AND the exact listing page isn't guaranteed stable either (no state is bound to a particular site layout) — so landing_page_url is deliberately the bare legislature domain, not a specific sub-page. discover_pdf_url's bounded crawl (generic election-vocabulary link-following, same-domain only) finds the real PDF from there every time, verified live: 3 real years (2024, 2022, 2020), both from the exact listing page AND from this bare-domain starting point, with default crawl bounds. Note: colorado's Blue Book is published by the LEGISLATURE, not the Secretary of State — verified the SOS's own domain does not lead to it at all (correctly returns no match rather than guessing). Parser verified against 2024's format (14/14 measures, 12/14 clean yes/no); 2022 uses a different sub-format for legislature-referred amendments that isn't handled yet (see ballot_measures_co.py's module docstring) — those measures are safely dropped, not guessed.

LA.description: 'Proposed Constitutional Amendments' guide, plain single-column text. All amendments are legislature-referred (Louisiana has no citizen-initiative process for constitutional amendments), so origin is fixed; the document publishes no explicit 'A YES vote means.../A NO vote means...' framing (only the ballot question itself) and no fiscal impact statement, so yes_means/no_means/fiscal_impact stay null rather than being inferred from the question's phrasing. Old site URLs 404'd after a site redesign; landing_page_url points at the current site. keyword requires BOTH terms present (a lone 'nov' also matches an unrelated 'November Presidential Election' link on the real page); exclude drops both the primary-election variant AND a same-year 'Statement of Proposed Constitutional Amendment...Summary' document that carries a confusingly similar link label but a different, unhandled layout. Verified against all 4 real general-election years on record (2026, 2024, 2022, 2020) — 2022's document has a per-page footer ('Prepared by the Louisiana Secretary of State N') and 2020/2022 both have a per-page running header ('<date> PROPOSED CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS'); both are stripped from the full joined text before splitting so a page-boundary-spanning amendment can't pick either up.

VA.description: Per-question 'Explanation for Proposed Constitutional Amendment' PDFs, one per question rather than one combined guide — discovered from the stable elections.virginia.gov/election-law/referenda/ index page, which links each question's own explanation page, which links that question's PDF in four languages (English has no language-code filename suffix). Verified live 2026-09-03 against all 3 real questions on the November 3, 2026 ballot (reproductive freedom, marriage, felony voting-rights restoration): 3/3 parse with a real Present-Law/Proposed-Amendment summary and the real ballot question text. No 'A YES vote means/A NO vote means' framing is published (same as Louisiana) and no fiscal-impact statement (constitutional amendments, not spending measures), so yes_means/no_means/fiscal_impact stay null. All Virginia amendments are General-Assembly-referred (no citizen-initiative process for amendments), so origin is fixed. Structurally different enough from every other state here (separate documents, not one combined guide) that it uses its own end-to-end fetch strategy (MULTI_DOCUMENT_STRATEGIES in ballot_measures_pdf.py, see ballot_measures_va.py) rather than the shared single-PDF pipeline.

MO.description: No PDF at all — the certified measures are published directly as HTML at a stable, evergreen url_pattern (sos.mo.gov/petitions/{year}ballotmeasures), verified live across 3 real cycles (2022/2024/2026, all 200 OK). The page carries both the state's August primary measures and its November general measures under two 'The following ballot measures ... <election>' headings; this strategy reads only the general-election section. Verified live 2026-09-03 against all 3 real measures on the November 3, 2026 ballot (reproductive rights/abortion repeal, a new state endowment fund, county sheriff elections): 3/3 parse with real 'Official Ballot Title' summaries, real fiscal notes, AND real 'A yes vote will.../A no vote will...' framing (Fair Ballot Language) — richer data than most states registered so far. Survived a real site inconsistency found in the process: Amendment 8's own heading paragraph sits as the last child of Amendment 7's <div>, not the first child of its own — this strategy flattens elements across div boundaries before splitting on the heading text itself, unaffected by that. Origin is read per-measure from its own 'Proposed by ...' line, not hardcoded fixed, since Missouri has a real citizen-initiative process for constitutional amendments (unlike LA/VA).
